entries.notes: The name Sơn Tây (meaning 'west of the mountain') originally referred to the Old Citadel area, derived from its geographical location relative to Tản Viên Peak.
The Sino-Vietnamese characters 山西 (Sơn Tây) appear on coins produced by the Sơn Tây Mint, as shown in the article's coin image.

Sơn Tây is located in the Red River Delta region, historically under Vietnamese polities. From the Lê dynasty restoration (1428) onward, this area was part of Đại Việt. Inferred from regional context; article mentions Nguyễn dynasty citadel.
The article references a citadel drawing from the Nguyễn dynasty period and a Sơn Tây Mint coin. Sơn Tây province was administered under the Nguyễn dynasty.
The 1884 photograph of Sơn Tây citadel corresponds to the French conquest of Tonkin. Sơn Tây fell under French colonial administration from 1883-1884.

After Vietnamese independence in 1945, Sơn Tây came under the Democratic Republic of Vietnam (North Vietnam). Inferred from regional history and the article's reference to Hà Tây province formation in 1965.

After reunification on 2 July 1976, Sơn Tây became part of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, administered under Hà Sơn Bình province, then transferred to Hanoi in 1978, then Hà Tây in 1991, then fully integrated into Hanoi in 2008.

The Red River Delta region where Sơn Tây is located was the heartland of Đông Sơn culture. The thousand-year-old villages suggest continuity of Vietnamese culture from this era, though this entry is inferred from regional context rather than specific archaeological finds at the site.
Vietnamese has been the dominant language of the Red River Delta region for over a millennium. Sơn Tây's name and the villages like Đường Lâm reflect Vietnamese linguistic heritage.
French was used as an administrative and elite language during the colonial period (1884-1945).
Vietnamese became the official state language after independence in 1945.
Buddhism has been a major religion in the Red River Delta since at least the 10th-11th centuries. Inferred from regional context for Vietnamese culture.

Taoism and Vietnamese folk religion were present alongside Buddhism in this region. The article mentions Và Temple dedicated to Tản Viên, a mountain deity associated with Vietnamese folk/syncretic religion.
French colonial presence from 1884 introduced Catholicism to the region. Inferred from general colonial history of Tonkin.

Sơn Tây is known for its thousand-year-old villages, implying settlement by at least the 11th century. The article references villages like Đường Lâm with vernacular architecture, suggesting early medieval habitation.

Sơn Tây functioned as a provincial capital (capital of Sơn Tây province) in the 19th-early 20th century, implying established town status by the Nguyễn dynasty period. The citadel drawing dates to the Nguyễn dynasty.
Sơn Tây was the capital of Sơn Tây province until 1965 when it merged with Hà Đông to form Hà Tây province.
Recognized as urban type III (đô thị loại III) on 13 April 2006; formally established as a city (thành phố) on 2 August 2007.
Demoted from city to town (thị xã) on 8 May 2009 when Hà Tây was absorbed into Hanoi.
Population of approximately 230,577 as of 2018, from the Vietnamese Wikipedia source.
